issues.title: Enroll passkey-first accounts without fabricated email identities
issues.description:
## Context / problem

The product requires genuine passkey-first accounts. AUTH-18 registers a key for an already authenticated mailbox account; current User/email DTOs and auth_users.email are non-null. AUTH-19 adds passkey authentication, and AUTH-20 covers management/recovery. An explicit email-free enrollment slice is needed to complete M03 without fabricating mailbox identities.

## Objective and expected behavior

A new user can create an account using a passkey without supplying email, prove possession of the resulting credential, sign in and reach the protected-user API. The server selects the opaque user ID and owns every bootstrap transaction. Existing verified-mailbox accounts retain their behavior and IDs.

## Technical scope / API and data

- Review and record an ADR for optional verified-mailbox identity and the passkey-first bootstrap, extending the existing four-crate feature modules.
- Add an explicit migration and typed public-contract changes for users without email; never insert placeholder addresses or treat display names as identity or authorization.
- Use the high-level WebAuthn service with required UV, exact RP/origin, bounded expiring server state, browser/purpose/realm binding and atomic one-time completion. Review discoverable-credential options against the pinned library; do not infer verified residency from an untrusted extension.
- Require a verified credential proof before issuing a fully authenticated session; reuse AUTH-19 authentication/counter/backup and method-provenance policy. Registration alone must not invent passkey authentication assurance.
- Define safe behavior of email/password/reset/lifecycle entrypoints for a user with no verified mailbox. Adding an email requires appropriate fresh account control plus mailbox proof; an already owned email is rejected without merging or transferring credentials.
- Keep ordinary composition gated until AUTH-20's stronger-account lifecycle/recovery policy is complete. Keep application permissions outside authentication.

## Security considerations

No matching-email linking, unverified-email login, mailbox-only stronger-account recovery or client-selected owner/realm/RP. Revalidate policy and ownership after locks. Bound anonymous enrollment, pending state and credential resources. Persist only the required verified credential/public metadata; redact private state and secrets. Review abuse, unfinished bootstrap cleanup and identity-creation races.

## Dependencies

AUTH-18 enrollment verifier/persistence and AUTH-19 genuine passkey authentication. This slice precedes AUTH-20's final management/recovery acceptance for both email-backed and email-free users. Use native Huly blocker relations. The M03 parent remains incomplete until all of these and real-device evidence pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- Real browser passkey-first enrollment, subsequent account-bound and discoverable authentication, and protected user retrieval work without an email address.
- Opaque user ID, credential ownership, RP/realm separation and required UV remain correct; no placeholder email is stored or returned.
- Replay/concurrent bootstrap has one successful account/session outcome. Failed persistence/audit rolls back identity, credential and consumed state together.
- Existing email-account data and APIs have explicit compatible migration/contract behavior with regression evidence.
- No-email and stronger-account users cannot enter an unintended email/password/reset fallback, merge on matching addresses, bypass fresh control or obtain an authenticated session from unverified bootstrap input.
- Documentation, generated OpenAPI, threat model, interoperability matrix and Huly evidence match actual support.

## Required tests

Real PostgreSQL upgrade/constraints/rollback/expiry/concurrency and cross-user/realm cases; real Chromium platform and roaming virtual-authenticator enrollment plus username-less authentication; wrong origin/RP/challenge/UV/signature, replay, changed owner and bootstrap/session confusion; optional-email serialization and existing mailbox-flow regressions. ## Context / problem
Make embedding and self-hosting reproducible.

## Objective and expected behavior
Documented public APIs and SDKs, no mandatory frontend runtime.

## Technical scope / API and data
Use the shared domain and explicit migrations; implement only the named boundary. Update docs/architecture/api-contract.md and the relevant domain entities if changed. Architecture: docs/architecture/overview.md; security: docs/security/threat-model.md; dependencies: docs/research/protocol-dependencies.md.

## Security considerations
Fail closed, tenant-isolate all reads/writes, keep secrets out of errors/logs, and prohibit email-based automatic identity linking. Protocol-specific rejection cases listed below are mandatory.

## Dependencies
See exported dependency keys and native Huly blocker relations. Milestone prerequisites must pass; unfinished dependency assessment is a release blocker, never an insecure fallback.

## Acceptance criteria
- Documented public APIs and SDKs, no mandatory frontend runtime.
- Required tests pass with recorded commands and evidence.
- Public docs state implemented behavior and residual limitations.
- No unrelated protocol/API or speculative abstraction introduced.

## Required tests
clean Docker deploy and independent example client smoke. Use real PostgreSQL for persistence/atomicity; external production credentials must not be required in default CI.

## Documentation impact
Update relevant architecture/guide, API schemas and interoperability evidence. Link implementation commit/PR in Huly.

## Explicit non-goals
Unrelated roadmap features, proprietary enterprise gates, custom cryptographic primitives, application business permissions and unsupported production-readiness claims.
